title: tunnel_auth check_time never advances last_now on the Ok path: rollback detection lags real time on a quiet gateway
description: Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-k8ix (P1). rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs check_time:419-430 updates self.last_now only on the fully-successful tails (accept_post:361, authorize_decapsulation:415), so the watermark is the time of the last SUCCESSFUL operation, not the last OBSERVED time. Python's mirror _observe_time (tunnel_auth.py:413) sets _last_now = now on EVERY non-rollback observation, including requests that later fail. On a low-traffic LoRa border router the watermark can lag real time unboundedly (and failing requests at real time never move it in Rust, while they would in Python); if the clock then rolls back to T with last_now <= T, the rollback is undetected and any entry that expired in real time but was not yet opportunistically purged authorizes decapsulation again - the captured-grant-cannot-rearm guarantee is void exactly when the gateway is quiet. Fix: set self.last_now = Some(now) on the Ok path of check_time (the tail assignments become redundant but harmless); keep the rollback path NOT updating last_now (retain the high-water).
close_reason: Fixed: check_time's Ok path now sets self.last_now = Some(now) on every non-rollback observation (tunnel_auth.rs), matching Python's _observe_time which sets _last_now on every observation. Watermark = last observed time, not last successful operation; rollback detection can no longer lag real time on a quiet gateway. Rollback path still retains (does not advance) the high-water. Verified: full gateway lib suite 221/221 (one pre-existing test rejected_wrong_authentication_signature_egress_expiry_and_replay_atomically used non-monotonic now values - 1 then 10_000 then 1 - which under correct semantics hits ClockRollback; reordered its asserts replay-before-expiry so time is monotonic, all original assertions preserved, none weakened); clippy clean; fmt applied.
